strengths: Strong and consistent empirical results with 10%+ absolute improvements across TextVQA, DocVQA, and V-Star Bench with generalization to multiple MLLM architectures
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including thorough ablation studies of all key components (pseudo-label pipeline, backbone depth, RPN depth, data efficiency)
Excellent data efficiency: achieves substantial improvements with only 10K training samples and demonstrates effective generalization

Well-designed pseudo-label generation pipeline with good empirical justification (Figure 3) and formal theoretical analysis (Appendix E) for why selective label assignment outperforms direct attention supervision
Superior efficiency trade-off with RoI prediction 1.5× faster than ViCrop while achieving better overall accuracy
Strong reproducibility with detailed implementation details, hyperparameters, layer configurations, algorithm pseudo-code, and layer selection rationale

Interesting counter-intuitive finding that self-generated responses produce better pseudo-labels than ground-truth, revealing important insights about representational consistency in self-distillation
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: combines established techniques (self-distillation, norm-based attention denoising, cross-attention RoI prediction) without introducing fundamentally new mechanisms
Key hyperparameters lack principled justification: τ_fg=0.2 and τ_bg=0.1 are empirically set with no sensitivity analysis or cross-dataset validation of threshold robustness
Pseudo-label generation uses heuristic bounding box approach for handling incomplete activation without exploring principled alternatives
Theoretical justification in Appendix E makes strong assumptions about noise models (CCN, additive activation) without empirical validation that these assumptions hold for MLLM attention
Missing failure case analysis: no discussion of when RoI prediction fails, what visual characteristics cause poor localization, or out-of-distribution robustness
Evaluation limited to VQA-style benchmarks; unclear how well method generalizes to other fine-grained visual understanding tasks beyond question-answering
Pseudo-label generation trained only on GQA and OCR-VQA—no analysis of domain-specific performance variation or how method performs on significantly different visual domains
Code availability claimed but URL blank ('Code is available at .'), preventing verification and reproducibility despite detailed documentation

strengths: Addresses a genuine efficiency-accuracy trade-off in MLLM fine-grained perception with clear problem motivation
Well-justified pseudo-label denoising pipeline with empirical analysis (Figure 3 histograms validating the foreground-background ambiguity problem)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 3 MLLM families, 8+ benchmarks, consistent 7-10% improvements on text-rich/vision-centric tasks
Exceptional data efficiency: achieves substantial gains with only 10K training samples, demonstrating strong generalization
Excellent reproducibility: detailed algorithms, hyperparameters, layer configurations, and theoretical analysis in appendices
Strong ablation studies systematically validating each component (pseudo-label generation, backbone depth, threshold sensitivity)
Practical efficiency gains: RoI prediction 1.5× faster than ViCrop, achieving better performance-throughput trade-off
Honest presentation: failure case analysis (spatial reasoning, incomplete activation) and fair comparison with external grounding models
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: combines established techniques (attention-based RoI, pseudo-labeling, self-distillation) with model-specific engineering rather than proposing fundamental new methods
Model-specific hyperparameter requirements: manual layer selection per architecture (Table 7) with no principled explanation reduces generalizability to new models

Diminishing returns on stronger models: Qwen2.5-VL shows only 2.7-3.0% improvement vs. 7-8% for LLaVA-1.5; DeepEyes sometimes outperforms on Qwen2.5-VL, suggesting decreasing efficacy with model capability
Fundamental unaddressed limitations: two-stage inference inherently loses spatial context; failures on spatial relationship reasoning indicate architectural ceiling not overcome by method
Attention signal assumption: entire approach depends on MLLM attention being aligned with visual grounding; robustness to different attention patterns not analyzed
Limited evaluation scope: only VQA tasks evaluated; generalization to other fine-grained perception tasks and video/3D unclear
Ad-hoc design choices: threshold values (τfg=0.2, τbg=0.1) determined empirically without principled justification; τnorm not ablated
Throughput reduction still substantial: 0.62× reduction despite 'efficient' claims; full system requires two forward passes with hidden training costs (152K samples)
